subject: RFP: Dedicated Inference Capacity — questionnaire and recommended reservation plan

Subject: RFP: Dedicated Inference Capacity Questionnaire — Horizon Analytics

Soojun / Redwood team,

Thanks for agreeing to respond to our procurement questionnaire. Attached is Horizon's formal Dedicated Inference Capacity Questionnaire — we need completed responses to GPU sizing, throughput targets, and reservation planning to evaluate vendors in the next procurement window.

High-level context:
- Use case: customer-facing generative assistant (chat + summarization) for enterprise customers.
- Peak expected concurrency: ~250 concurrent sessions (concurrent open chats).
- Typical request: 1-2 user messages + 1 assistant generation; average prompt + response = ~350 tokens.
- Desired SLO: 95th percentile response latency < 400ms for generation up to 1024 tokens.
- Target go-live: January 2027; procurement evaluation ends mid-November.

Questions in particular where we need explicit numbers: per-GPU expected throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) for the models you recommend, recommended GPU types and counts for a committed baseline (monthly reserved) to meet the targets above, autoscaling/burst approach (how you propose covering 20-40% unexpected traffic), and any notes on quantization/precision tradeoffs that would materially affect latency/cost.

Please return by Wednesday 4 Nov if possible (we may ask follow-ups).

Thanks,
Michael Dunn
Head of Procurement, Horizon Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: RFP: Dedicated Inference Capacity Questionnaire — Horizon Analytics

Hi team,

I populated the Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_20261102.xlsx with our recommendations and included an executive "capacity-summary-20261102.pdf". High level summary below; the workbook contains the per-model benchmark runs and assumptions (avg prompt tokens, generation length distribution, temperature settings, tokenization overhead).

Executive recommendations (baseline + burst):
1) Preferred baseline (latency-first): Allocate 6 x H100 80GB (primary pool)
   - Reason: consistent low-latency for generative workloads at 1k token context; H100 shows the best tokens/sec in our tests for the model families Horizon is considering (open-llama/llama2-family and two moderate-sized instruction-tuned variants).
   - Expected throughput per GPU (conservative): ~10k tokens/sec, which translates to ~25–30 requests/sec for average generation length 350 tokens.
   - SLO coverage: 6 x H100 covers sustained 150–180 req/s with 20% headroom and meets 95th <400ms for 1024-token generation in our internal tests at your expected temperature settings.

2) Cost-reduced baseline (mixed pool): 4 x H100 (primary) + 4 x A100 80GB (secondary)
   - Publishable throughput per A100: ~6k tokens/sec (quantized FP16 path); latency slightly higher but still within 95th <450ms at 1024 tokens for this mixed configuration.
   - Use-case: if Horizon is sensitive to committed spend but still needs predictable throughput, keep mixed pool and route latency-sensitive traffic to H100 pool.

3) Quantization guidance and model variants:
   - For best cost-performance, we recommend 8-bit GPTQ/QLoRA-style quantization for models >=13B, which reduces memory and improves batching efficiency with minimal quality regression for instruction-following tasks.
   - For latency-sensitive production generation (95th targets), keep FP16 or fused kernel paths on H100; quantized variants can be used for background batch jobs or lower priority inference.

4) Burst strategy (to cover +20–40% spikes):
   - Reserved baseline should include a 20% buffer. For additional burst, Redwood Dedicated supports two modes: (a) soft burst to on-demand dedicated nodes in the same region (short cold-start ~45–90s) and (b) spill to our hosted multi-tenant pool (fastest but subject to multi-tenant routing policies).
   - Recommended plan: reserve 6 H100 + commit an additional 2-node burst buffer as part of the contract (warm standby A100 or H100 depending on price negotiation). For >40% spikes, use hosted overflow with routing policy to degrade to a quantized model variant.

5) Autoscaling and routing policies:
   - Autoscale by queue length + latency SLA. Maintain per-route latency SLO monitoring; when 95th latency approaches threshold for two consecutive minutes, begin routing non-critical requests to quantized variant and/or spill to hosted pool.

6) High-availability and rollout notes:
   - We recommend distributing the baseline across 3 availability zones with at least one H100 in each to avoid AZ outage exposure.

A few benchmark caveats: our numbers assume sequence length distribution provided in workbook and the following runtime settings: continuous batching enabled, KV cache persistence, and temperature defaults at 0.7 for chat generation. If Horizon increases average generation length or enables heavy sampling (temp>0.9, top-p wide), throughput per GPU will drop ~15–30% depending on sampling complexity.

I've attached the workbook with sheets: assumptions, per-GPU benchmarks, recommended reservation sizes (monthly commit), and a cost delta table for H100 vs A100 vs mixed pools.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_20261102.xlsx, capacity-summary-20261102.pdf

Let me know if you want me to convert the conservative tokens/sec numbers to a per-route QPS table for Horizon's specific 95th targets — I can do that quickly.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@horizon-analytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFP: Dedicated Inference Capacity Questionnaire — Horizon Analytics

Elaine — quick answers below, happy to jump on a short call if you want deeper context.

1) Tokens/sec delta (1024 context):
   - H100 80GB FP16 (our standard low-latency path): ~10k tokens/sec (baseline numbers used in the workbook).
   - H100 80GB 8-bit quantized: ~9k–9.5k tokens/sec (5–10% throughput reduction observed in our bench runs for the highest-quality GPTQ/QLoRA builds). Quality tradeoff minimal for instruction-following tasks but depends on the exact model and calibration set.
   - A100 80GB FP16: ~6k tokens/sec. A100 8-bit quantized: ~5.5k tokens/sec (similar 8–10% delta).

   Note: the delta is smaller for smaller models (<13B) and larger for very large models where kernel fusion and memory bandwidth differences matter. The workbook has the per-model bench sheet showing raw run outputs and standard deviations.

2) Burst/warm-standby policy and worst-case ramp:
   - Worst-case cold-start for a full node allocate + model load (cold) is ~90–120s depending on model size and parallel download time.
   - Warm-standby approach we support: keep node allocated but paused with model already loaded into GPU memory (we charge a lower nightly standby rate for this). With this mode, handover/traffic acceptance is sub-5s (near-instant).
   - Recommended contractual approach for your SLA: include 1 warm-standby per AZ as part of the committed burst buffer. This gives effectively immediate capacity for the first surge and reduces billing surprises.

If Horizon wants, we can create two quote lines: (A) 6 H100 baseline + 2 warm-standby nodes (preferred for latency) and (B) mixed baseline (4 H100 + 4 A100) with 2 warm standbys. I'll add the warm-standby pricing details to the workbook and re-send.

- Rishi
